# Program Overview

The **BYU AI Foundry** pairs a sponsoring organization with a faculty-guided team of BYU
Marriott students for a full academic year. The team takes on one real, open-ended business
problem and delivers an AI-enabled solution to it.

[**Submit a Project →**](https://byu.capsource.app/)

## Engagement Structure

| Component | Details |
|-----------|---------|
| **Duration** | 8 months, 2 semesters |
| **Period** | September 2, 2026 – April 14, 2027 |
| **Team size** | 4–6 students per project |
| **Student effort** | 8–12 hours per week, per student |
| **Sponsor commitment** | ~1 hour per week |
| **Location** | Remote, with optional on-site visits |
| **Sponsorship fee** | $22,000 per project |
| **Intellectual property** | Sponsor retains all deliverables and IP |

## Academic Credit

Students enroll in the AI Foundry Lab, cross-listed as **MBA 693R** and **STRAT 490R**, for
3.0 credit hours per semester and 6.0 across the year. Teams mix MBA and senior undergraduate
students by design.

## Who Is on Your Team

Every team carries three roles:

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| **Client lead** | Your single point of contact. Runs the weekly call, sends the weekly update, owns scope conversations |
| **Builders** | The analysis, modeling, and software |
| **QC lead** | Reviews everything before it reaches you. Owns the quality standard |

A faculty director oversees every engagement and reviews all four milestones independently of
the client.

## The Year in Four Milestones

| Milestone | Date | What you receive |
|-----------|------|------------------|
| **M1: Problem definition and framework** | October 16, 2026 | A written problem statement you sign off on, the decision criteria, and how success will be measured |
| **M2: Working prototype** | December 11, 2026 | Something that runs, on real or realistic data, with the logic documented |
| **M3: Validated model** | February 19, 2027 | Sensitivity analysis, stated assumptions, explainable outputs, known limitations |
| **M4: Final delivery** | April 9, 2027 | Executive summary, decision tool or dashboard, handoff documentation, and the repository |

## What Sponsorship Covers

The $22,000 fee covers faculty oversight and direction, student team time across two semesters,
software and API costs, data and tooling access, program administration, and the final delivery
showcase.

## What We Deliver

The Foundry builds business decision systems. Typical deliverables:

- Strategy assessment and validation
- Decision frameworks with explicit criteria and thresholds
- Scoring and prioritization models
- Forecasting and predictive analytics
- Financial models, including NPV, sensitivity, and scenario analysis
- Optimization under real capital, capacity, and resource constraints
- Executive decision dashboards and prototype applications
- Executive-ready synthesis and recommendations

Every deliverable carries an explainability requirement: your team can walk you through which
assumptions drive each recommendation and what would have to change for the answer to change.

## What We Do Not Do

Being clear about this saves everyone time.

- **Production software.** We deliver working prototypes and models, not systems hardened for
  your production environment.
- **Staff augmentation.** This is not a way to get cheap analyst hours on your existing backlog.
- **Work that is already scoped and specified.** If you know exactly what you want built, hire a
  contractor. The Foundry is for open-ended problems where the answer is not known yet.
- **Regulated or safety-critical deliverables.** Nothing we produce should be relied on as a
  clinical, legal, financial, or regulatory determination without your own review.

## How This Differs from the Engineering Capstone

BYU's engineering capstone programs build physical and embedded systems: CAD, prototypes, PCBs,
firmware, security assessments. The AI Foundry builds business decision systems.

If your question is "how do we build this thing," that is an engineering capstone. If your
question is "which things should we build, in what order, and how would we know," that is the
Foundry.
